title: Hometown Bandwidth
style: alt-country, pedal steel, brushed drums, warm electric guitar, subtle modular synth, gritty male vocal, americana with electronic undercurrent, 96 bpm, road song
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
My hometown's got a tower on the hill
Blinking red against the prairie chill
When I was young I thought it was a star
Now I know it tells the world where we are

[Verse 2]
Dad worked thirty years on the line
Mom raised four kids and a garden vine
Every letter from a soldier overseas
Came down through wires in the cottonwood trees

[Chorus]
My hometown's got a bandwidth all its own
A frequency you can hear from miles from home
It hums in the diner, it hums in the church
It's the sound of a place that's worth what it's worth

[Verse 3]
Got a girl who can name every band on the dial
She drives me down county roads for a while
We park where the signal hits just right
And we listen to the world all night

[Chorus]
My hometown's got a bandwidth all its own
A frequency you can hear from miles from home
It hums in the diner, it hums in the church
It's the sound of a place that's worth what it's worth

[Bridge]
You can leave but the tower keeps blinking
You can run but the wire keeps thinking
You can change your name and change your town
But the signal will always find you down

[Outro]
Blinking red, blinking red
Over the cornfields, over my head
Blinking red, blinking red
The hometown bandwidth, alive and ahead
